These emit visible light through thermal emission, electrical excitation or luminescence. source_reviews.independent_solution: Yes. The hot, dense solid filament of an ordinary incandescent lamp emits a broad continuous thermal spectrum, including visible light and infrared. source_reviews.independent_solution: One valid transmission-grating arrangement is source -> narrow entrance slit -> collimator lens -> plane diffraction grating -> observing telescope or focusing lens and detector. Put the slit at the collimator's focal plane so the grating receives a parallel beam. Mount the grating in this beam where the prism would have been, with its rulings parallel to the slit for the usual arrangement. For normal incidence, place the grating plane perpendicular to the incident beam. Observe nonzero diffraction orders at angles to the incident direction using a rotatable telescope, or use collecting optics and a suitable screen or sensor to record the separated slit images. With grating spacing d, normal-incidence principal maxima satisfy d sin(theta) = m lambda. Thus wavelengths are separated in nonzero orders; the undeviated zero order is not a dispersed spectrum. For the same admissible positive order, a longer wavelength appears at a larger angle from the normal.

source_reviews.independent_solution: For ordinary elemental emission analysis, introduce the sample into a suitable energetic source that vaporizes/atomizes it and excites its atoms or ions, for example a sufficiently hot flame or an electric arc or spark. Excited species then emit characteristic photons as they return to lower energy states; collect that light with a spectrometer. The excitation method must suit the material and produce enough line intensity to observe. Merely making a bulk solid glow is insufficient as a general answer because its thermal continuum does not by itself isolate the desired characteristic atomic lines.

source_reviews.independent_solution: Ordinary window glass selectively attenuates ultraviolet radiation: it strongly suppresses shorter ultraviolet wavelengths, including much of UVB, while a substantial portion of longer-wavelength UVA can pass through ordinary uncoated glass. The transmitted sunlight therefore has reduced and altered ultraviolet content, not necessarily zero ultraviolet content. Absorption and transmission depend on wavelength as well as glass composition, thickness and coatings. Transparency to visible light does not establish either complete transparency or complete opacity across the whole ultraviolet band.

source_reviews.independent_solution: They mainly indicate constituents of the Sun's observable atmosphere, including line-forming photospheric layers, not a direct measurement of the deep interior. Broad continuum light from deeper, hotter visible layers travels through line-forming layers whose atoms and ions absorb selectively at their characteristic transition wavelengths. Those missing or reduced spectral intensities identify the relevant atmospheric species.

source_reviews.independent_solution: Radio waves: an antenna coupled to an appropriate receiving/tuned circuit converts the incident electromagnetic field into an electrical signal; a meter or oscilloscope displays it, and a recording oscilloscope or data recorder can retain it. Visible light: a photographic camera/plate/film records exposure, or a photodiode or image sensor with electronic readout detects it and can record it with storage. X-rays: an appropriate X-ray photographic film, an ionization detector, a semiconductor X-ray detector, or a scintillator coupled to a photodetector can detect exposure; film or an attached electronic recorder provides a retained record. Suitable devices are selected for the radiation's interactions with the detector material and its operating wavelength/energy range.
